title: Vigil run
description: One extraction + matching run for one Patient. The Trial Briefing is rendered from this JSON. Vigil imports it into the Clinical Record (unverified) and a Match Run.

trial_export_id.description: The export_id from the trial export file used; every trial below must come from it

target_cancer_diagnosis_ref.description: ref of the Cancer Diagnosis the trials are matched for (the target Condition)

conditions.description: Comorbidities and other diagnoses that are not cancers (cancers go in cancer_diagnoses)

ref.description: Run-local id, e.g. cd1, bm3; used to link facts

doc_id.description: File name of the input document, exactly as uploaded

quote.description: Verbatim text from the document that supports the value (copy, do not paraphrase)

cancer_diagnoses.description: Every cancer, current or past (a past melanoma counts: it is an 'other malignancy' for trials)

gaps.description: Facts trials commonly need that the documents do not give (e.g. ECOG not formally rated, MET amplification not tested)

snapshot.description: Page 1 of the Briefing: the condition snapshot, each paragraph built only from clinical_record facts

anyOf.description: The most time-sensitive factor for trial eligibility, if any, stated as a fact plus the questions it raises for the treating team

trials.description: Trials shown in full: POTENTIALLY_ELIGIBLE and NEEDS_INFORMATION only, at most 8, ordered by match_state, then site access, then fewest UNKNOWN

mechanism.description: What the intervention targets and how, from the trial record only (e.g. 'EGFR×cMET bispecific ADC; IV every 3 weeks'). Never rated against the Patient.

anyOf.description: Copied from the trial export (straight-line from the Patient's suburb)
This Patient's most recent anticancer therapy
The trial's brain-metastasis rule, quoted or closely summarised

criteria.description: Every gating eligibility criterion, parsed from the trial text

raw_text.description: The criterion verbatim from the trial export

result.description: MET always means 'does not stand in the way': for an exclusion, MET means the exclusion does not apply

items.description: refs of clinical_record facts relied on; empty when UNKNOWN for lack of data

summary.description: Observations only (criteria, gating items, access). Never recommend, never 'pursue', never 'eligible'.

not_shown.description: Trials considered but not shown in full: every EXCLUDED trial with its deciding criterion, and any surplus beyond 8
